pull.title: refactor: Use NotNull for CreateNewBlock and pimpls
pull.body:
Current code uses nullable smart pointers for some stuff that is never null. This is perfectly fine, but a bit confusing:

* When reading the code, it is not clear which pointer is nullable or never null.
* Pointers that are never null still have confusing null checks (with possible error handling return branches), which are always dead in coverage reports or when applying mutation testing.
* While some places have the redundant null checks on pointers that are never null, other places do not, which adds to the confusion.

Clarify this at compile-time by using `NotNull` (or a plain reference)

refactor: Return NotNull from CreateNewBlock

A nullptr is never returned, so the existing code is confusing, because
it either has redundant and dead checks for a nullptr, or the existing
code is "missing" them.

Fix both issues by marking the type as NotNull at compile-time.

comments.body: In fa0e2f600bf901f7c8d4e1574b4d3ad1e80a5cff _refactor: Return NotNull from CreateNewBlock_: this might be worth its own commit, e.g. https://github.com/Sjors/bitcoin/commit/d5591a9143cae9829fb1c8a375b88b4297ff7070

In fa0e2f600bf901f7c8d4e1574b4d3ad1e80a5cff _refactor: Return NotNull from CreateNewBlock_: having to add `util::NotNull{...}` is a bit tedious. But if you forget, the error is clear enough:

```
note: explicit constructor is not a candidate
   49 |     constexpr explicit NotNull(U&& u) noexcept(...)
      |                        ^
```

(the current code is fine, I don't think we should make the constructor implicit)
Yes, being explicit is intentional, since the `NotNull` ctor acts as an `Assert`  on the value.
